rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Sahl reports that the Prophet tied an imam’s leadership to accountability, complementing the verse’s appointment of a khalifa: good conduct benefits him and worshippers, while wrongdoing falls on him.
rows.anchor: إِنِّي سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ يَقُولُ

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Umm Salama reports that during his final illness the Prophet repeatedly urged care for prayer and those under one's right hand, until he could barely speak.
rows.anchor: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ كَانَ يَقُولُ فِي مَرَضِهِ الَّذِي تُوُفِّيَ فِيهِ

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Anas reports that prayer and care for those under one's right hand made up most of the Prophet’s counsel as he was dying.
rows.anchor: كَانَتْ عَامَّةُ وَصِيَّةِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم حِينَ حَضَرَتْهُ الْوَفَاةُ

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet’s final words urged observance of prayer and care for those under one's right hand.
rows.anchor: كَانَ آخِرُ كَلاَمِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar recounts that the Prophet comforted him over their poverty, saying that the Hereafter belongs to them while worldly abundance belongs to the Persian and Byzantine rulers.
rows.anchor: حَدَّثَنِي عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ، قَالَ دَخَلْتُ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ وَهُوَ عَلَى حَصِيرٍ

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Ibn Umar reports that God privately confronts and forgives the believer’s sins, while the unbeliever or hypocrite is publicly exposed, citing the verse about those who lied against their Lord.
rows.anchor: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ يَقُولُ

none: The report concerns funeral-prayer takbirs and gives no relevant link to 6:128.
The report warns about the lasting consequences of speech, without a relevant link to 6:128.

rows.speaker: سعد
rows.claim: Saʿd reports that this verse was revealed about six believers, including him, Ibn Masʿud, Suhayb, ʿAmmar, al-Miqdad and Bilal, after Quraysh demanded that they be sent away.
rows.anchor: عَنْ سَعْدٍ، قَالَ نَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ فِينَا سِتَّةٍ فِيَّ وَفِي ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Anas reports that on the Resurrection believers seek relief from Adam, Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus, then Muhammad intercedes repeatedly and God admits groups within limits He sets.
rows.anchor: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ قَالَ

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Anas also reports the Prophet saying that people with even an atom’s weight of good in their hearts and faith in God’s oneness will be brought out of Hell.
rows.anchor: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ قَالَ

words: وَمَا مُحَمَّدٌ إِلاَّ رَسُولٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ الرُّسُلُ
rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha recounts that after the Prophet’s death some denied he had died; Abu Bakr affirmed it and recited 3:144, after which Umar said it was as if he had only then read the verse.
rows.anchor: عَنْ عَائِشَةَ، قَالَتْ لَمَّا قُبِضَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ

none: The report compares unjustly killing a believer with the end of the world; it does not address 14:38.
The report concerns the Dajjal and does not address 14:38.
The report compares worldly life to a mosquito’s wing and does not address 14:38.
The report compares worldly life to a discarded goat kid and does not address 14:38.
The report concerns grief, patience and compassion at a child’s death, with no relevant link to 35:28.
The report describes divine sleeplessness and the veil of light, without a relevant link to 36:69.
The report concerns equal enforcement of theft penalties and gives no relevant link to 36:69.

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet’s warning that helping murder a believer even by half a word brings one before God marked as despairing of His mercy, underscoring the gravity of sin.
rows.anchor: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet, as transmitted by Zayd and affirmed by Ubayy, Ibn Masʿud and Hudhayfa, teaches that qadar must be believed: events are fixed, and without this belief even immense charity is not accepted.
rows.anchor: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ يَقُولُ

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that when Quraysh polytheists disputed predestination with the Prophet, verses 54:48–49 were revealed.
rows.anchor: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ جَاءَ مُشْرِكُو قُرَيْشٍ يُخَاصِمُونَ النَّبِيَّ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ فِي الْقَدَرِ
